title: Chess, But SCP-106 Traps You In His Pocket Dimension
summary: Two-board chess vs Stockfish. SCP-106 ('the old man') wanders the main board starting on g4; every piece that comes in contact with him (adjacent) is teleported to a random empty square on a secondary 'pocket dimension' board. Each turn a player makes one move on the main board AND one move on the pocket board (if they have pieces there). Pieces escape the pocket dimension by reaching its centre, which teleports them to a random empty square of the main board. Pawns teleported to the pocket board often land near promotion and become queens. Kings can be sent there too. Narrator wins game one with a discovered pawn-attack checkmate.
rules: Main board: standard chess start, player White vs Stockfish (3600) Black.
Neutral SCP-106 starts on g4 and wanders one square per round [step size inferred].
After he moves, every piece (either colour, kings included) adjacent to him is teleported to a random empty square on the pocket-dimension board.
Each turn the mover makes one move on the main board and one move on the pocket board (if they have pieces there).
Pieces on the pocket board move/capture/promote normally; pawns keep their direction and can promote there.
A piece that moves onto the centre square(s) of the pocket board is teleported to a random EMPTY square of the main board (it may land en prise).

A capture on the main board sends... both capturer and captured? No - transcript: 'We do get captured by the black knight and both of those pieces do teleport to the secondary board' (the knight captured next to SCP-106 and both were then adjacent) [ambiguous].
Checkmate can occur with the king on either board [inferred].
win_condition: Checkmate Stockfish's king (won via discovered pawn-attack mate on the main board).
